claims.claim: Modern labor tools and mute robots have eased the twofold labor of life, but this lack of manifest necessity makes it more difficult to recognize human subjection to necessity, which is a precondition for freedom.
qualifications: human freedom is won in never wholly successful attempts to liberate oneself from necessity
claims.supporting_excerpt: It is true that the enormous improvement in our labor tools—the mute robots with which homo faber has come to the help of the animal laborans ... has made the twofold labor of life ... easier and less painful than it has ever been. ... Man cannot be free if he does not know that he is subject to necessity, because his freedom is always won in his never wholly successful attempts to liberate himself from necessity.

claims.claim: Tools and instruments are products of work and parts of the world of use objects rather than products of labor or consumption.
claims.supporting_excerpt: Tools and instruments which can ease the effort of labor considerably are themselves not a product of labor but of work; they do not belong in the process of consumption but are part and parcel of the world of use objects.

definitions.definition: Improved labor tools provided by homo faber to assist the animal laborans.
Speaking instruments, historically used to designate slaves in ancient households who served the man of action and the endless process of life.

distinctions.distinction: Workmanship tools produce something beyond mere use and have a predictable, controllable end with a finished product, whereas household instruments serve the endless process of living and consumption.

must_not_be_lost: The fundamental distinction that tools belong to work and use objects rather than labor and consumption.
The philosophical danger that making necessity less manifest impairs human freedom.
parsed.segment_function: Analyze the role of tools, instruments, and robotic assistance in relation to labor and work, contrasting modern technological improvements with ancient institutions like slavery and discussing the limitations of tools regarding the endless process of life and biological necessity.
